facts.fact_text: The applicant was a former member of the Armenian Parliament.
The applicant was a member of the political council of an opposition party.
The applicant was a supporter of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's candidacy at the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election.
The applicant was an active participant in the protest rallies, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins at Freedom Square.
The applicant was an active participant in the protest rallies, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins at Freedom Square.
The applicant spent the night of 23 to 24 February 2008 at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. he and two of his friends, A.Sis. and V.K., were driving home from the rally at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. the car in which the applicant, A.Sis. and V.K. were travelling was blocked on Teryan Street in Yerevan by another car.
According to the applicant, masked gunmen emerged from the blocking car and demanded that the applicant and his friends get out of their car.
According to the applicant, he was thrown to the ground and searched but nothing was found.

According to the applicant, he and his companions A.Sis. and V.K. were forced into the blocking car and taken to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC).

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC) on 24 February 2008 at around 11.30 a.m. by operative police officers of the PDFOC.
According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the PDFOC on suspicion of carrying illegal arms and ammunition.
At 11.45 a.m. on 24 February 2008 the applicant was subjected to a search at the PDFOC by police officers in the presence of two attesting witnesses.
The record of the applicant's search at the PDFOC indicated that a spring baton had been found in the applicant's coat pocket.
The record of the applicant's search at the PDFOC indicated that the applicant had stated that the baton belonged to him and that he carried it for self-defence.

The applicant, in his application to the Court, contested the circumstances of his being searched at the PDFOC and alleged that no arms or other prohibited items had been found as a result of that search.
The applicant alleged that after the search at the PDFOC he was taken to another room where a police officer produced a baton, saying that it had been found in his car.
The applicant alleged that he denied that the baton belonged to him or that it had ever been in his car.
The applicant alleged that police officers persuaded him to admit that the baton had been found during his personal search, saying that he, as a member of the Hunters' Union, was allowed to own it.

The applicant alleged that police officers threatened that if he refused to confess, they would record that the baton had been found during the personal search of A.Sis. and V.K., who, not being members of the Hunters' Union, would be prosecuted.
The applicant alleged that under such circumstances he was compelled to confess that the baton belonged to him.
The applicant alleged that only after his compelled confession were the two attesting witnesses called in and a record of his personal search drawn up.
At an unspecified hour on 24 February 2008 the applicant's car was searched at the PDFOC and a Makarov-type pistol was found.
On 24 February 2008 one of the PDFOC officers addressed a report to the Head of the PDFOC.

According to the PDFOC officer's report, on 24 February 2008 at 11 a.m. an anonymous call had been made to the PDFOC stating that a Lexus-model black car was parked at the crossroads of Teryan and Koryun Streets in Yerevan and that its passengers were armed.

According to the PDFOC officer's report, an operative group of police officers of the PDFOC had immediately set off to the scene and taken into custody the Lexus-model black car and its passengers: the applicant, A.Sis. and V.K.
According to the PDFOC officer's report, a spring baton had been found when the applicant was searched.
According to the PDFOC officer's report, a Makarov-type pistol was found on searching the applicant's car.
A statement was taken from the applicant in which he submitted that he had spent the previous night at Freedom Square at a rally in support of Mr Ter-Petrosyan.
The applicant submitted in his statement that in the morning on his way home his car had been stopped on Teryan Street by police officers who had taken him and the other passengers to the PDFOC.
The applicant submitted in his statement that the Makarov pistol belonged to him and was a registered weapon granted to him in 1994 by the Minister of Defence of Armenia.
The applicant submitted in his statement that he had the necessary documents showing that he carried the Makarov pistol legally.
The applicant submitted in his statement that the baton found during his search also belonged to him and he carried it for self-defence.
On 24 February 2008 the applicant and the materials concerning his case were transferred from the PDFOC to Kentron Police Station of Yerevan for further inquiry.

An investigator at Kentron Police Station decided to order that the applicant undergo a forensic toxicological-chemical examination to detect use of drugs, reasoning the need for such examination by the fact that a baton had been found in the applicant's possession.
The investigator at Kentron Police Station ordered a forensic examination of the Makarov pistol found in the applicant's car.
The forensic expert examining the Makarov pistol found that it lacked a hammer, rendering it ineffective and therefore not to be considered a firearm.
At 11 p.m. on 24 February 2008 the applicant was taken by police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S. of Kentron Police Station to the National Bureau of Examinations.
At the National Bureau of Examinations the applicant underwent the assigned forensic toxicological-chemical examination, which revealed no traces of drugs in his body.

Upon return from the National Bureau of Examinations, police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S. reported to the Chief of Kentron Police Station that on the way back the applicant had started complaining of being treated unlawfully and threatened them with violence.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., upon reaching Kentron Police Station the applicant had disobeyed their order to step out of the car.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., the applicant pushed police officer K.H. when leaving the car and started a scuffle with him.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., the applicant refused to enter the police building and punched police officer K.H. several times in the chest.
According to police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., the applicant was forcibly pushed into Kentron Police Station by the three officers, where he continued threatening them with violence.
The applicant alleged that no incident involving resistance or assault on police officers had ever happened upon his return to Kentron Police Station.
According to the applicant, as the car pulled up at Kentron Police Station, he got out of the car upon an order from one of the police officers and they accompanied him into the building.
According to the applicant, the only thing he said when he got out of the car was to tell the police officers that his arrest was unlawful.

The applicant alleged that a number of his relatives and friends, one of his future defence lawyers and a journalist had been standing near Kentron Police Station at the time he was brought back from the forensic examination, having gathered there expecting his release.
On 25 February 2008 the investigator took statements from police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., who confirmed their earlier reports.
On 25 February 2008 the investigator decided to institute a criminal case under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (non-life or health-threatening assault on a public official).

The decision to institute a criminal case stated that on 24 February 2008 around 11 p.m. the applicant, who had been brought in from the crossroads of Koryun and Teryan Streets of Yerevan on suspicion of using drugs and illegal possession of arms, was transported to the National Bureau of Examination to give samples.

The decision to institute a criminal case stated that on the way back from the National Bureau of Examination, the applicant, first in the car and then in the front yard of Kentron Police Station, disobeyed the lawful orders of the police officers, insulted them and assaulted them in a non-life-threatening way by punching one of the police officers.

On 25 February 2008 at 1.35 a.m. a record of the applicant's arrest was drawn up stating that the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having committed an offence under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 25 February 2008 police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S. were questioned as witnesses and confirmed their earlier statements.
The applicant was questioned as a suspect but refused to testify or answer any questions.
The applicant declared that he was a victim of political persecution and that the charge against him was trumped up.
On 25 February 2008 police officer K.H. underwent a forensic medical examination which did not reveal any injuries on his body.
On 27 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The decision formally charging the applicant stated that on 24 February 2008 at around 11.30 p.m. in front of Kentron Police Station the applicant had threatened the police officers and, in defiance of their lawful orders, inflicted non-life-threatening violence on police officer K.H. by punching him in the chest.
On 27 February 2008 the applicant was brought before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan (the District Court).

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan examined the investigator's application seeking to have the applicant detained for a period of two months on the ground that, if he remained at large, he could commit a new offence, abscond or obstruct the investigation.
The applicant submitted before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that the application for his detention was unsubstantiated.

The applicant submitted before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that he had not resisted or punched the police officers and would not have been able to do so since he had been handcuffed.
The applicant submitted before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that he was a war veteran with many military awards, no criminal record and a permanent place of residence.
The applicant declared before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that the case against him was politically motivated.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan decided to allow the investigator's application for the applicant's detention, finding that, if the applicant remained at large, he could commit a new offence, abscond or obstruct the investigation.
On 29 February 2008 the investigator decided to order a forensic examination of the spring baton found in the applicant's possession.

The forensic expert concluded that the spring baton was a factory-produced mace which could be characterised as a striking-crushing cold weapon (սառը զենք), based on its overall appearance, measurements, structure and relevant literature.
On 29 February 2008 the results of the toxicological-chemical examination were produced and no traces of drugs were found in the applicant's body.
On 1 March 2008 in the early morning a police operation was conducted on Freedom Square where several hundred demonstrators were camping.
As a result of the police operation on 1 March 2008, Freedom Square was cleared of all demonstrators, resulting in clashes between the demonstrators and the police.

On 1 March 2008 criminal proceedings were instituted regarding the events at Freedom Square on the grounds that the leaders of the opposition and their supporters had organised unlawful demonstrations, incited disobedience and committed violence against the police.
Further details regarding the criminal proceedings instituted on 1 March 2008 are set out in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia, no. 23086/08, § 15, 20 September 2018.
Later on 1 March 2008 the situation in Yerevan deteriorated and rallies continued in a number of streets until early in the morning of 2 March 2008.
The rallies on 1-2 March 2008 involved clashes between protesters and law enforcement officers.
The events of 1-2 March 2008 in Yerevan resulted in ten deaths, including eight civilians.
The events of 1-2 March 2008 in Yerevan resulted in numerous injured persons.
Following the events of 1-2 March 2008, a state of emergency was declared by the President of Armenia.

On 2 March 2008 another set of criminal proceedings was instituted on the grounds that the leaders of the opposition and their supporters had organised mass disorder in the streets of Yerevan, including murders, violence and other reprehensible acts.
Further details regarding the criminal proceedings instituted on 2 March 2008 are set out in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia, no. 23086/08, § 17.
On 2 March 2008 both sets of criminal proceedings instituted on 1 March 2008 and 2 March 2008 were joined and examined under case number 62202608.
On 11 March 2008 the investigator decided to join the applicant's criminal case to case no. 62202608.
The decision to join the applicant's criminal case to case no. 62202608 stated that the applicant had also taken part in organising and conducting the unlawful demonstrations.

On 12 March 2008 the investigator, referring to case no. 62202608, prohibited the applicant's contact with the outside world, including close relatives, the media and any other person, on the ground that such contact might obstruct the investigation.
On 2 April 2008 the applicant went on a hunger strike, demanding that the authorities stop his political persecution and release him from detention.
On 15 April 2008 the investigator applied to the court to have the applicant's detention extended.
In the application to extend the applicant's detention, the investigator referred to the materials of criminal case no. 62202608 and the progress made in the investigation of that case.

The investigator's application to extend detention stated that sufficient information had been obtained suggesting that the applicant, after the defeat of Mr Ter-Petrosyan in the presidential election, having joined a group of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's like-minded followers and conspired with them to usurp State power in violation of Armenia's Constitution, had actively participated in the implementation of the mentioned criminal plan.

The investigator's application to extend detention stated that it was necessary to carry out further investigative measures to clarify the circumstances of the applicant's involvement in the criminal act in question.
On 21 April 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan allowed the investigator's application and extended the applicant's detention by two months.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan extended the applicant's detention on 21 April 2008 taking into account the nature and dangerousness of the imputed offence and the fact that the applicant, if he remained at large, could abscond, obstruct the investigation or avoid criminal responsibility and punishment.
In extending the applicant's detention on 21 April 2008, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan made a reference to the investigation conducted into criminal case no. 62202608.

On 26 April 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal against the detention extension decision, arguing inter alia that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision was unreasoned and the risks of his absconding or obstructing the investigation were unsubstantiated.

On 8 May 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the detention extension, finding that the circumstances on which the applicant's detention was based persisted, since there was still a high risk that the applicant could obstruct the investigation and abscond.
On 23 May 2008 the investigator questioned police officer S.H., who was said to be on guard duty at Kentron Police Station on the night of 24 February 2008.
On 3 June 2008 the investigator questioned police officer A.H., who was said to be on guard duty at Kentron Police Station on the night of 24 February 2008.

Police officer S.H. stated that he had heard loud noises from outside Kentron Police Station, stepped outside and seen police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S. holding the applicant by his arms, trying to push him into the police station.

Police officer S.H. stated that the applicant was disobeying, showing resistance to the officers and trying to free himself, while shouting and making threats, and had eventually been pushed inside the station where he continued making threats.

Police officer A.H. stated that he had been inside Kentron Police Station and seen a person, whom he later recognised as a former minister, held by his arms by police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., brought inside the station where he briefly threatened to have the officers' heads smashed and then calmed down and sat down.
Both police officers S.H. and A.H. stated that police officer K.H. had sat down when inside Kentron Police Station, holding his hand to his chest and saying that the applicant had punched him.
On 15 June 2008 the investigator applied to the court to have the applicant's detention extended once more, again making reference to the materials of criminal case no. 62202608.

In the application to extend the applicant's detention on 15 June 2008, the investigator added that, following a number of investigative measures, no sufficient evidence had been obtained directly implicating the applicant in the commission of the criminal act investigated in case no. 62202608.
On 18 June 2008 the applicant's criminal case was disjoined from case no. 62202608 as it was apparently ready for trial.

On 19 June 2008 the General Prosecutor's Office wrote to the investigator dealing with the applicant's case, drawing his attention to the fact that the applicant had been charged only under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The General Prosecutor's Office noted that the applicant's actions had also contained elements of an offence envisaged by Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal carrying of a cold weapon) and instructed the investigator to bring new charges.
On 20 June 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan extended the applicant's detention by 20 days, namely until 15 July 2008, on the same grounds as previously.
On 24 June 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal against the detention extension decision of 20 June 2008, raising the same arguments as previously.
On 26 June 2008 the investigator decided to bring a new charge against the applicant under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The decision to bring a new charge under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code stated that a spring baton had been found in the applicant's coat pocket as a result of the personal search conducted upon bringing him to the police station on 24 February 2008.
On 7 July 2008 the investigation into the applicant's criminal case was completed and the case was referred to the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for trial.

On 9 July 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal decided to leave the applicant's appeal of 24 June 2008 without examination on the ground that the investigation had been completed and the case had been referred for trial.
On 14 July 2008 a judge of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan who had taken over the applicant's criminal case decided to set the case down for trial.
On 22 July 2008, during the first hearing, the applicant requested to be released from detention.
The applicant argued at the hearing on 22 July 2008 that his detention authorised by a court had expired on 15 July 2008.

The applicant argued at the hearing on 22 July 2008 that the judge had failed to address the issue of his detention when deciding to set the case down for trial on 14 July 2008, in violation of Articles 293 and 300 of the Armenian Code of Criminal Procedure.

On 22 July 2008 the judge took a decision stating that the question of the applicant's continued detention had been examined on 14 July 2008 when adopting the decision to set the case down for trial and it had been decided to leave the applicant's detention unchanged.

The judge stated on 22 July 2008 that as a result of a typographical error, the paragraph concerning the applicant's detention had not been reflected in the operative part of the decision of 14 July 2008, which was to be read as containing the phrase 'to leave the applicant's detention unchanged'.
At the next hearing on 28 July 2008 the judge presented the parties with the decision of 22 July 2008 and dismissed the applicant's request for release.

On 17 September 2008 another judge of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan who had taken over the applicant's case decided to set the case down for trial and also ruled to leave the applicant's detention unchanged.

In the course of the trial the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan summoned for questioning police officers K.H., E.P., A.S., S.H. and A.H., who maintained their statements against the applicant.
After police officers S.H. and A.H. gave their testimony, the applicant requested additional time to prepare for their questioning.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request for additional time to prepare for questioning of police officers S.H. and A.H. on the ground that the applicant and his defence lawyers had had enough time to prepare themselves.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan stated that it was ready to allow a request for additional preparation time in the future if it were substantiated.
At the next court hearing the applicant lodged a similar request, seeking to summon and question police officers S.H. and A.H.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan announced that it would examine the applicant's request to summon police officers S.H. and A.H. after the applicant's questioning but it appears that it never revisited that question.
The applicant pleaded not guilty and contested the factual allegations against him at trial.
The applicant lodged several requests with the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan seeking to call witnesses on his behalf.
The applicant requested that a number of persons be summoned as witnesses, including S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y., who were his relatives, political supporters and one journalist.

The applicant submitted that S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. had gathered at Kentron Police Station and had been standing at the entrance when he was brought back by police officers from the forensic examination and could confirm that no incident had taken place as he left the car and entered the police building.
The applicant requested that A.Sis. and V.K., who had been kept at Kentron Police Station on the night from 24 to 25 February 2008, be summoned as witnesses.

The applicant submitted that A.Sis. and V.K. had witnessed from their cell window how he had been escorted into the police building and later had heard no shouts or sounds of protest when he had been escorted through the lobby inside the building.
In support of the requests to call witnesses, the applicant's lawyer submitted records of statements which the lawyer had taken from those persons containing their relevant submissions.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. on the ground that the case file contained no information about those persons.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon A.Sis. and V.K. on the ground that it was not necessary to call those persons since the materials of the case contained sufficient information to draw appropriate conclusions.

The applicant's lawyer requested the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan to admit as evidence the records of the statements taken from the persons the applicant had sought to call as witnesses.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan granted the applicant's lawyer's request and the statements were included in the case file.
On 19 November 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant guilty as charged.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code to two years' imprisonment.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code to a fine in the amount of 300,000 Armenian drams (AMD).

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant had illegally carried a spring baton (mace) characterised as a striking-crushing cold weapon, which was found in his coat pocket and seized during his personal search on 24 February 2008.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant, having found out about the need to take samples from him, became agitated, started complaining and, on the way back to Kentron Police Station, made threats of retribution against the accompanying police officers who were performing their official duties.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that near the entrance to Kentron Police Station, police officer K.H. and witnesses E.P. and A.S. ordered the applicant to step out of the car and to enter the police building, and the applicant disobeyed their lawful order.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that after police officer K.H. repeated the order, the applicant first pushed and then, using non-life and health-threatening violence, pulled and punched police officer K.H. several times in the chest, causing him physical pain.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant was thereafter forcibly taken inside the lobby of Kentron Police Station, while he continued his threats addressed at the police officers.

In reaching its findings, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan relied on the statements of the police officers, the record of the applicant's bringing-in, the record of the applicant's search, the conclusions of the forensic expert characterising the baton as a striking-crushing cold weapon, and the applicant's statement of 24 February 2008 in which he had admitted that the baton belonged to him.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant's arguments and the materials submitted by him to be unreliable, in conflict with the circumstances of the case and provided by persons who had close relations with the applicant, were not impartial and aimed to protect him.
On 9 December 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal against the judgment of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had failed to assess properly the evidence and ignored his submissions in support of his innocence.
In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had based its findings solely on the statements of police officers.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had refused to hear the persons whom he had sought to call as witnesses on his behalf.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had deprived him of the opportunity to question witnesses against him, namely police officers S.H. and A.H.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant alleged that the true reason for his prosecution and conviction was his being an opposition activist and to prevent his participation in the opposition demonstrations, arguing that he had been discriminated against on the basis of his political views.
On 27 January 2009 the Criminal Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan and dismissed the applicant's appeal.

The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the arguments relied on in the applicant's appeal, including the impossibility to question in court police officers S.H. and A.H., could not serve as a valid ground for quashing the judgment as they were not indicative of a substantial violation of the criminal process.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the indictment and the conviction were based on sufficient evidence proving the applicant's guilt.

The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the applicant's allegations that the true reason for his prosecution was his political activism and participation in the opposition demonstrations were unsubstantiated, as the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had been guided by the law, legal awareness, inner conviction and the evidence obtained and examined in court.
On 27 April 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal on points of law, raising similar arguments as in his appeal of 9 December 2008.
On 15 June 2009 the Court of Cassation of Armenia declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.
Later in June 2009 the applicant was granted amnesty and released from prison after having served more than half of his sentence.

On 27 January 2009 the Criminal Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan and dismissed the applicant's appeal.
On 27 April 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal on points of law, raising similar arguments as in his appeal of 9 December 2008.
On 15 June 2009 the Court of Cassation of Armenia declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.
The applicant was a supporter of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's candidacy at the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election.
The applicant was an active participant in the protest rallies, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins at Freedom Square.
The applicant spent the night of 23 to 24 February 2008 at Freedom Square.

According to the PDFOC officer's report, on 24 February 2008 at 11 a.m. an anonymous call had been made to the PDFOC stating that a Lexus-model black car was parked at the crossroads of Teryan and Koryun Streets in Yerevan and that its passengers were armed.
A statement was taken from the applicant in which he submitted that he had spent the previous night at Freedom Square at a rally in support of Mr Ter-Petrosyan.
The applicant submitted in his statement that in the morning on his way home his car had been stopped on Teryan Street by police officers who had taken him and the other passengers to the PDFOC.
The applicant alleged that no incident involving resistance or assault on police officers had ever happened upon his return to Kentron Police Station.
According to the applicant, as the car pulled up at Kentron Police Station, he got out of the car upon an order from one of the police officers and they accompanied him into the building.
According to the applicant, the only thing he said when he got out of the car was to tell the police officers that his arrest was unlawful.

The applicant alleged that a number of his relatives and friends, one of his future defence lawyers and a journalist had been standing near Kentron Police Station at the time he was brought back from the forensic examination, having gathered there expecting his release.

The decision to institute a criminal case stated that on the way back from the National Bureau of Examination, the applicant, first in the car and then in the front yard of Kentron Police Station, disobeyed the lawful orders of the police officers, insulted them and assaulted them in a non-life-threatening way by punching one of the police officers.
The applicant declared that he was a victim of political persecution and that the charge against him was trumped up.
The applicant declared before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that the case against him was politically motivated.
On 11 March 2008 the investigator decided to join the applicant's criminal case to case no. 62202608.
The decision to join the applicant's criminal case to case no. 62202608 stated that the applicant had also taken part in organising and conducting the unlawful demonstrations.

The investigator's application to extend detention stated that sufficient information had been obtained suggesting that the applicant, after the defeat of Mr Ter-Petrosyan in the presidential election, having joined a group of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's like-minded followers and conspired with them to usurp State power in violation of Armenia's Constitution, had actively participated in the implementation of the mentioned criminal plan.

In the application to extend the applicant's detention on 15 June 2008, the investigator added that, following a number of investigative measures, no sufficient evidence had been obtained directly implicating the applicant in the commission of the criminal act investigated in case no. 62202608.

The General Prosecutor's Office noted that the applicant's actions had also contained elements of an offence envisaged by Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal carrying of a cold weapon) and instructed the investigator to bring new charges.
The applicant pleaded not guilty and contested the factual allegations against him at trial.
The applicant lodged several requests with the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan seeking to call witnesses on his behalf.
The applicant requested that a number of persons be summoned as witnesses, including S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y., who were his relatives, political supporters and one journalist.

The applicant submitted that S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. had gathered at Kentron Police Station and had been standing at the entrance when he was brought back by police officers from the forensic examination and could confirm that no incident had taken place as he left the car and entered the police building.
The applicant requested that A.Sis. and V.K., who had been kept at Kentron Police Station on the night from 24 to 25 February 2008, be summoned as witnesses.

The applicant submitted that A.Sis. and V.K. had witnessed from their cell window how he had been escorted into the police building and later had heard no shouts or sounds of protest when he had been escorted through the lobby inside the building.
In support of the requests to call witnesses, the applicant's lawyer submitted records of statements which the lawyer had taken from those persons containing their relevant submissions.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. on the ground that the case file contained no information about those persons.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon A.Sis. and V.K. on the ground that it was not necessary to call those persons since the materials of the case contained sufficient information to draw appropriate conclusions.

The applicant's lawyer requested the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan to admit as evidence the records of the statements taken from the persons the applicant had sought to call as witnesses.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan granted the applicant's lawyer's request and the statements were included in the case file.

In reaching its findings, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan relied on the statements of the police officers, the record of the applicant's bringing-in, the record of the applicant's search, the conclusions of the forensic expert characterising the baton as a striking-crushing cold weapon, and the applicant's statement of 24 February 2008 in which he had admitted that the baton belonged to him.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant's arguments and the materials submitted by him to be unreliable, in conflict with the circumstances of the case and provided by persons who had close relations with the applicant, were not impartial and aimed to protect him.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had failed to assess properly the evidence and ignored his submissions in support of his innocence.
In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had based its findings solely on the statements of police officers.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had refused to hear the persons whom he had sought to call as witnesses on his behalf.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had deprived him of the opportunity to question witnesses against him, namely police officers S.H. and A.H.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant alleged that the true reason for his prosecution and conviction was his being an opposition activist and to prevent his participation in the opposition demonstrations, arguing that he had been discriminated against on the basis of his political views.

The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the arguments relied on in the applicant's appeal, including the impossibility to question in court police officers S.H. and A.H., could not serve as a valid ground for quashing the judgment as they were not indicative of a substantial violation of the criminal process.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the indictment and the conviction were based on sufficient evidence proving the applicant's guilt.

The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the applicant's allegations that the true reason for his prosecution was his political activism and participation in the opposition demonstrations were unsubstantiated, as the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had been guided by the law, legal awareness, inner conviction and the evidence obtained and examined in court.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that a number of those officials, as well as several opposition activists, were arrested on seemingly artificial charges, which left the impression that their prosecution was politically motivated.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that according to the Helsinki Association of Armenia, a total of 14 persons were arrested and placed under investigation in the period from 20 to 29 February 2008.
